columns: in Messed Up Dress Up's rules
rows: recognized player intents: direction ::= north | south | east | west, intent ::= move⟨direction⟩ | collect

the Event sum: Pull(Side), PullBoulder(Side), PullHatch(Int), PullThing(Int), FallPit(Int), WayOut(Int), Way(Dir), with Dir = + N + NE + E + SE + S + SW + W + NW. Taking a way out of a square, by whichever control, goes through one door handler (worldWalk) and reaches the rule as the one intent Way(d), as the paper's five interfaces all end in move⟨direction⟩.
game mechanics: a game step ⟨G₁; intent⟩ ⟶ ⟨G₂; resp⟩

a room's rule, on_event : (Globals, Event) -> Cmd: the state it is told (Globals) and the intent give a response as data, which the game then carries out (its new state). Done alone is the paper's failure, a way that leads nowhere; GoSquare(c, r, side, Done) its success.
contextual interface: only the intents that make sense in this state

the sums themselves: before them, a direction was any text, and a rule could be asked about "up" (the Fumola check had a case for it); now it cannot be said. The paper calls this the subtractive side of an interface's syntax. What is offered in a given state (a lever only where there is one) is still the game's JS, not a type.
a completeness conjecture: every state and intent has a next state and a response
proved, in a PL, by cases
checked, not proved: on every push, every case the game can give each room (32,761 for Hazel, 20,649 for Fumola) has an answer, and the same answer in all three languages (^ticket(567)).
a log of intents and responses, as structured terms

a response is already a little straight-line program, each command with the rest after it (Flip(L, SetPit(0, true, Done))), which the game runs in order; a log of Events and Cmds would be the paper's trace, not kept yet.
players composing actions into their own programs (BOTS, Cube Composer)
the editable Hazel and Fumola boxes: a player (or M and N) can rewrite a room's rule in the game and play it at once, so the mechanics, not only the intents, become a language players write in.
